subject: RE: Follow-up + next tests: observability & inference comparison vs hyperscalers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: next steps on observability & perf tests

Samir — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Great to hear about the latency-sensitive ranking workflow and the need to unify observability across inference endpoints. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

High-level recap:
- Primary use case: real-time ranking (<= 120ms p99 target) serving ~300 qps during peak.
- Current infra: mixed — some inference on AWS SageMaker endpoints, some on GCP Autopilot; teams are frustrated by opaque per-request cost and limited tracing across systems.
- Evaluation goals: latency/throughput comparison, KV-cache effectiveness, and end-to-end observability (trace linkage from application -> model -> infra).

Proposed next tests (we recommend a two-tier approach):
1) Latency/throughput smoke test (2h): run identical workload against your current SageMaker endpoint and a Redwood-hosted test endpoint. We'll collect p50/p95/p99, token cost, and CPU/GPU utilization.
2) Observability pass (1 day): enable distributed traces and per-request token breakdowns; provide a dashboard showing request-level latency, model/table lookups, and cache hit rates.
3) Integration test (canary, 48h): route 5-10% of traffic to Redwood with automatic fallback.

Differentiators we plan to show:
- Unified trace IDs across app -> inference -> infra (we’ll attach an example trace).
- Per-token cost breakdown and model-variant routing to reduce tail latency.
- Built-in KV/prefix caching that can eliminate repeated prefix compute for your ranking prompts.

Logistics / asks from your side:
- Provide an API key for the SageMaker test endpoint (read-only execution logs) or a short-lived role we can assume for perf metrics.
- Confirm a 2-hr slot for the smoke test this week (we suggested Wed 11/18 10–12 PST).
- Anyone else who should be on the canary approval (CC'ing Neha & Rishi here to help scope).

I've attached our benchmark summary and a draft mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx). I've also shared a Drive folder with the demo recording and test artifacts.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if you want to walk through the test plan live.
—Marissa
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: next steps on observability & perf tests

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying Qs from our infra/engineering leads: 

1) When you say "unified trace IDs", will Redwood auto-propagate trace context from our app (we're on OpenTelemetry currently), or do you require custom instrumentation?
2) For the latency smoke test, can you run both a raw token-only latency and end-to-end including our preprocessor? The preprocessor adds ~10–20ms on average and we want to isolate model latency.
3) For cost comparisons vs hyperscaler endpoints (SageMaker/GCP), what metrics will you provide beyond per-token cost? We want to see GPU utilization and amortized cost per request.

We can do Wed 11/18 10–12 PST for the smoke test — Priya will coordinate with our infra team for the credentials.

Also looping Priya for procurement concerns; if the results look good we'll need a draft SOW and an estimated committed monthly spend to share with finance.

—Samir
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
samir.gupta@acme.com

Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: next steps on observability & perf tests

Samir — great questions, answered inline below.

1) Trace propagation: Redwood supports OpenTelemetry context propagation out of the box (W3C traceparent) — no custom instrumentation required for basic traces. For richer application-specific spans we recommend adding a small client-side span wrapper; we've included an example snippet in the shared Drive.

2) Latency breakdowns: we will report (a) pure model-response latency (token-generation p50/p95/p99), (b) end-to-end service latency including network and your preprocessor, and (c) system-level metrics (GPU utilization, GPU memory, CPU). We'll attach dashboards after the smoke test.

3) Cost metrics: per-token cost, amortized cost per request (GPU-hours/request), and an estimate of 95th-percentile unit cost with and without prefix/KV caching. We will also surface any savings from model-variant routing (e.g., using smaller quantized variant for low-criticality requests).

Planned deliverables after smoke test:
- Dashboard with p50/p95/p99 for both endpoints + GPU utilization heatmap.
- Trace examples showing span linkage from your API -> Redwood -> model execution.
- CSV of per-request token counts and latency for offline analysis.

Logistics for Wed 11/18 10–12 PST:
- Priya: can you share a short-lived ARN or API key for the SageMaker test endpoint (read-only exec logs)? If easier, we can use a sample record replay (we can host a replay harness if providing creds is difficult).
- We'll provision a Redwood test endpoint and share curl/postman examples — ETA Tue evening.

Next: I'll schedule a 30m checkpoint at 11/18 11:30 PST to review initial numbers.

—Marissa
